auraIntro: Explorer, Cartwheel Galaxy was reshaped by a violent head-on galactic collision, creating expanding shockwaves of star formation.
overview: The Cartwheel Galaxy (ESO 350-40) is a famous ring galaxy located 500 million light-years away in the constellation Sculptor.
formation: Formed roughly 500 million years ago when a small companion galaxy punched directly through the center of a larger spiral galaxy.
structure: A ring galaxy spanning 150,000 light-years across. It features an inner ring surrounding the core and a outer ring expanding at 217,000 mph.
discoveryHistory: Discovered in 1941 by Fritz Zwicky, who described it as 'one of the most complicated structures waiting for an explanation.'
observationTips: Extremely distant at 500 million light-years; imaged extensively by Hubble and JWST's NIRCam instruments.
funFacts: Created when a smaller companion galaxy pierced straight through the center of a spiral galaxy like a pebble in a pond.
The outer ring is expanding at over 217,000 mph (350,000 km/h), plowing into surrounding gas and sparking starbursts.
JWST images revealed faint optical 'spokes' connecting the inner hub to the outer rim.

cards.body: Like a stone dropped in water, the collision sent a gravitational shockwave outwards, sweeping up interstellar gas into an expanding ring of newborn stars.
bulletPoints: Ring expanding at 217,000 mph into intergalactic medium.
Spokes contain silicate dust filaments and young star clusters.
Companion intruder galaxy visible trailing in space nearby.
